sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 斐庇里得斯从雅典跑去召唤斯巴达人来马拉松参战，然后他又跑了回来。

sentences.zh: 而斯巴达人说他们会晚点到。

sentences.zh: 然后他遇到了

sentences.zh: 潘就在那里。

sentences.zh: 所以我正在这样写，把神明重新放回历史中。

sentences.en: And it's kind of like rewilding history because suddenly all kinds of things make sense.
sentences.zh: 这有点像给历史重新野化，因为突然之间各种事情都说得通了。

sentences.en: So I've been kind of thinking about this, that I think part of the appeal of it almost is entering a world in which these gods are possible.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在思考这一点，我认为它的吸引力有一部分几乎在于进入一个这些神明切实存在的世界。

sentences.en: And there's something about their glamour, their mystique, the kind of way in which then they behave terribly.
sentences.zh: 而且它们的魅力、神秘感，以及它们表现得极其糟糕的那种方式，

sentences.en: Maybe it's appealing to children.
sentences.zh: 也许这对孩子们很有吸引力。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: There's something of that.
sentences.zh: 确实有那么一点意思。

sentences.en: I think you may be right.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的。

sentences.en: And I like your dinosaur dragons idea.
sentences.zh: 我也很喜欢你那个关于恐龙和龙的想法。

sentences.en: I think there is this sense that I had, and I'm sure you had, as a child when reading Greek mythology, that somehow there was a,
sentences.zh: 我认为确实有一种感觉，我和你一样，在小时候阅读希腊神话时，总觉得有一种，

sentences.zh: 它追溯到某种真实或某种纯粹而正确的东西。

sentences.en: Whereas a single authored fantasy world like Tolkien's or Narnia or any other, while it can be terrific fun, doesn't have that
sentences.zh: 而像托尔金或纳尼亚或其他任何单一作者创作的奇幻世界，虽然可以带来极大的乐趣，却没有那种

sentences.en: sort of authenticity, that sense of it belonging to something real.
sentences.zh: 所谓的真实感，没有那种属于某种真实事物的质感。

sentences.en: There's a weight, isn't there, Stephen?
sentences.zh: 很有分量感，对吧，斯蒂芬？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think it's kind of a weightiness that there's a sense of rootedness, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一种厚重感，我想，有一种根基感。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But actually, I want to press you on this.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我想在这个问题上追问你。

sentences.en: I'm so glad you brought it up because in our house, I have a nine-year-old.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你提起这个，因为我们家里有一个九岁的孩子。

sentences.en: So you are a constant presence.
sentences.zh: 所以你是一个无处不在的存在。

sentences.en: I mean, you're in our ears all the time through Harry Potter, through The Hobbit, the Sherlock Holmes audio books, which you did.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，通过《哈利·波特》、《霍比特人》以及你录制的《福尔摩斯探案集》有声书，你一直都在我们的耳边。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering whether, I mean, some of those things have a kind of mythic quality.
sentences.zh: 我在想，我的意思是，其中一些作品具有某种神话般的特质。

sentences.en: So Sherlock
sentences.zh: 所以，比方说福尔摩斯

sentences.en: Holmes, for example, I mean, he's become a kind of mythic character.
sentences.zh: ——我的意思是，他已经变成了一个类似神话般的角色。

sentences.en: He's accumulated, like a sort of old boat.
sentences.zh: 他就像一艘老船那样累积了各种东西。

sentences.en: He's got all these kind of carbuncles on, all these sort of, you know, he's more than purely the creation of Arthur Conan Doyle, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他身上长满了这种藤壶般的东西，所有这些，你知道的，他不仅仅是阿瑟·柯南·道尔纯粹创造的产物，对吧？

sentences.en: And do you think there are other modern equivalents that have become mythic in the same way as Holmes' characters?
sentences.zh: 你认为还有其他现代的同类角色，能以和福尔摩斯相同的方式变成神话吗？

sentences.en: I think Holmes is a pretty special example.
sentences.zh: 我认为福尔摩斯是一个相当特殊的例子。

sentences.en: I was thinking about this not long ago, about how many characters could you express in a game of Pictionary quite so quickly as Sherlock Holmes.
sentences.zh: 不久前我还在想这个问题：在《看图猜词》游戏中，你能像表现福尔摩斯那样迅速地画出多少个角色？

sentences.en: You'd have a looking glass and a deer stalker and a pipe and instantly, wherever you were in the world, they could say, Sherlock Holmes.
sentences.zh: 你只需要画一面放大镜、一顶猎鹿帽和一个烟斗，瞬间，无论你在世界的哪个角落，人们都会说：福尔摩斯。

sentences.en: And, you know, you could do it, I suppose, with Charlie
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我想查理

sentences.en: Chaplin as a film image character and maybe with the circles for the ears of Mickey Mouse.
sentences.zh: 卓别林作为电影形象角色也可以做到，也许米老鼠标志性的圆形耳朵也可以。

sentences.en: So you're moving towards the logo side of characters there.
sentences.zh: 所以你在那里正在走向标志性角色的方向。

sentences.en: But there is no question that Sherlock
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，福尔摩斯

sentences.en: Holmes has extraordinary reach through cultures all over the world.
sentences.zh: 在世界各地有着非同寻常的影响力。

sentences.en: And one can look for answers as to why that might be.
sentences.zh: 人们可以寻找为什么会这样的答案。

sentences.en: I suppose the most obvious one is that we all want Sherlock Holmes in the same way I suppose we want Jeeves.
sentences.zh: 我想最显而易见的一个原因就是，我们都渴望拥有福尔摩斯，就像我们渴望拥有吉夫斯一样。

sentences.en: You know, there is this idea of wouldn't it be wonderful to have a friend, a mentor, a wise teacher who saw things and knew things and could
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这里有一种想法：如果能有一个朋友、一个导师、一个能看清事物并知晓一切、能够给我们

sentences.en: advise us and yet, you know, be a friend and not be an emperor or in some way a terrible boss, you know, but just someone there who could just solve everything for us.
sentences.zh: 建议，同时又是朋友而不是什么暴君或可怕的老板，你知道的，只是一个能为我们解决一切问题的人，那该有多好。

sentences.en: And it's interesting because there isn't that much of an archetype.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为这种原型并不多见。

sentences.en: I mean, you could argue that Jeeves and so on is an archetype, you know, the servant that's wiser than his master goes back through Volpone
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以争辩说吉夫斯之类的是一种原型，你知道的，比主人更聪明的仆人这个设定可以追溯到小庞

sentences.en: and, you know, Ben Johnson and Goldoni and all that, and right back to Terence and Roscius and those, you know, Roman plays, all full of stupid masters, aren't they, who are kind
sentences.zh: 和本·琼森、哥尔多尼以及所有人，一直追溯到泰伦斯和罗西乌斯以及那些罗马戏剧，里面到处都是愚蠢的主人，对吧？他们某种程度上

sentences.en: of equivalents of a Bertie Worcester, but to have a Sherlock Holmes figure, I suppose the closest is Odysseus in a way, because one of the things you can say about the Trojan
sentences.zh: 相当于伯蒂·伍斯特，但要说拥有一个福尔摩斯式的人物，我想最接近的在某种程度上是奥德修斯，因为关于特洛伊战争，

sentences.en: War, again, without being too sort of prescriptive about it, is that it's mankind playing out
sentences.zh: 同样，不要对此过于教条地说，你可以说它是人类在演绎

sentences.en: what mankind is, you know, this first test of this greatest war that's ever been, these two civilizations clashing and more soldiers and more ships and more resources being put
sentences.zh: 人类本身，你知道的，这是这场有史以来最伟大战争的第一次考验，两大文明的碰撞，更多的士兵、更多的战舰和更多的资源被投入

sentences.en: into this fight.
sentences.zh: 这场战斗中。

sentences.en: And what's going to win it?
sentences.zh: 什么能赢得胜利？

sentences.en: There's Ajax and Diomedes and all these remarkable Hector, these great fighters, Penthesilea and Memnon and all these amazing warriors, but they don't win it.
sentences.zh: 有埃阿斯、狄奥墨德斯以及所有这些杰出的赫克托耳、这些伟大的战士、彭忒西勒亚和门农以及所有这些惊人的勇士，但他们并没有赢得战争。

sentences.en: What wins it is deceit, cunning, tricky.
sentences.zh: 赢得胜利的是欺骗、狡猾和诡计。

sentences.en: Those are the human qualities.
sentences.zh: 这些才是人性的品质。

sentences.en: And it is, you know, I mean, Nietzsche wanted us to look at Dionysus and Apollo as the two
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，尼采曾希望我们把狄奥尼索斯和阿波罗视为希腊精神背后的两种

sentences.en: principles that are behind the Greek spirit and so on in terms of, you know, harmony, golden order, reason, numbers, prophecy, all the beauties of the Apollonian way.
sentences.zh: 原则，就和谐、黄金秩序、理性、数字、预言以及阿波罗式道路的所有美感而言。

sentences.en: And then underneath that, of course, the frenzy, the appetite, the addiction, the instinct and impulse of the
sentences.zh: 而在那之下，当然，则是狂热、欲望、沉溺、狄奥尼索斯式生存方式的本能与冲动。

sentences.en: Dionysian way of being.
sentences.zh: 狄奥尼索斯式生存方式。

sentences.en: But also there is in between Hermes and his descendant Odysseus, where sheer trickery, lying, deceit, storytelling, which is, of course, another aspect of Hermes,
sentences.zh: 但同时，在赫尔墨斯和他的后代奥德修斯之间，还有纯粹的诡计、谎言、欺骗和讲故事——当然，这也是赫尔墨斯另一个方面的职责，

sentences.en: one of his responsibilities.
sentences.zh: 他是他的职责之一。

sentences.en: He's the god of storytellers as well as of liars.
sentences.zh: 他既是故事讲述者之神，也是骗子之神。

sentences.en: And we're storytellers as our liars, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们讲故事也就是在撒谎。

sentences.en: So maybe behind that glory is an impish truth about humanity.
sentences.zh: 所以也许那份荣耀背后，隐藏着一个关于人性的顽皮真相。

sentences.en: The Icelandic and Norse saga makers we're kind of familiar with, but I was reading ages ago, and I can't remember who, so I may have got it very wrong.
sentences.zh: 冰岛和北欧的萨迦创作者是我们比较熟悉的，但我很久以前读过——我不记得是谁写的了，所以我可能记得很错——

sentences.en: But I was reading that, as it were, on the hillside at the end of the battle, there would be two bonfires and around one would be a
sentences.zh: 但我读到过，仿佛在战斗结束的山坡上，会有两处篝火，一处周围是一群

sentences.en: group of people listening to the saga maker, who would tell how Hengist had destroyed 40 people
sentences.zh: 听萨迦创作者讲述的人，他会讲述海恩吉斯特如何用

sentences.en: with, you know, his sword and killed another 20 just by strangling them and how heroic he was.
sentences.zh: 他的剑消灭了40人，又仅靠掐脖子杀死了另外20人，以及他是多么英勇。

sentences.en: Then around the other bonfire would be the glee man, who would tell how Hengist had actually not managed to strap his sword and had fallen over.
sentences.zh: 然后另一处篝火周围则是游吟诗人，他会讲述海恩吉斯特其实没能系好剑结果摔倒了。

sentences.en: But he had fallen over on top of two of the enemy and squashed them.
sentences.zh: 但他摔倒在两个敌人身上把他们压扁了。

sentences.en: And he would tell a satirical comic version of the battle.
sentences.zh: 他会讲述一个关于这场战斗的讽刺滑稽版本。

sentences.en: And in a strange sort of way, the Trojan War is like that.
sentences.zh: 从某种奇怪的角度来看，特洛伊战争就是这样的。

sentences.en: There is this noble roster of extraordinary heroes and their incredible courage and their skill with swords and spears and bows and arrows and chariots and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 这里有一份高贵杰出英雄的名册，有他们不可思议的勇气、他们使用剑、长矛、弓箭和战车等武器的精湛技艺。

sentences.en: But then there is this deceitful, wicked figure, this delightful, cunning Odysseus, who strokes his chin and thinks up ways of using deceit to win the war.
sentences.zh: 但随后又出现了这个诡诈邪恶的人物、这个机敏狡猾的奥德修斯，他抚摸着下巴，想出各种利用欺骗来赢得战争的方法。

sentences.en: And that is what wins it, followed by appalling violence, of course.
sentences.zh: 而这才是赢得战争的关键，当然，随之而来的是骇人听闻的暴力。

sentences.en: But that's, it's as if, because I think one of the things about Greek myth is that Greeks must have, and I hate, I know it's wrong to say must have,
sentences.zh: 但这，就好像——因为我认为希腊神话的特点之一在于，希腊人一定曾经——虽然我讨厌，我知道说“一定曾经”是不对的，

sentences.en: we don't know what they thought, but I would be astonished if the Greeks weren't astonished by themselves.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道他们的想法，但如果希腊人没有对自己感到惊叹，我会感到震惊。

sentences.en: That's to say that they must have noticed how unusual though, as you've got out of the archaic into the historical classical Greek era, they must have noticed that they now had the
sentences.zh: 也就是说，当你们从古风时期跨入历史上的古典希腊时代时，他们一定已经注意到，他们现在拥有了

sentences.en: writing that the Phoenicians had given them, the Cadmian alphabet, as they called it.
sentences.zh: 腓尼基人传给他们的文字，也就是他们所说的卡德摩斯字母。

sentences.en: So that was fine.
sentences.zh: 所以这很好。

sentences.en: But they'd build up a civilization that was actually better than the one across the sea, the Egyptian one that existed for thousands of years, and barely changed in that time.
sentences.zh: 但他们建立的文明实际上比海对岸那个存在了数千年且在此期间几乎没有改变的埃及文明还要优秀。

sentences.en: It takes an Egyptologist to say, oh, that particular pylon is 3,000 years old, that one is 5,000 years old, but that's 2,000 year difference.
sentences.zh: 必须要埃及古物学者才会说，哦，那个特定的塔门有3000年历史，那个有5000年历史，但那是2000年的差距。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, if you go back 2,000 years from now, you're in the year 1020, you're 40 years before the Battle of Hastings, and it's a very different world.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的意思是，如果从现在起倒回2000年，你就回到了1020年，那是黑斯廷斯战役前40年，那是一个非常不同的世界。

sentences.en: Whereas the Egyptians stayed the same, and the Greeks appeared to be the first civilization
sentences.zh: 而埃及人保持不变，希腊人则似乎是第一个相信进步、

sentences.en: that believed in progress, that wanted to learn new things, and change, and add, and adapt,
sentences.zh: 渴望学习新事物、渴望改变、增加、采纳、适应，并在文明、政体、政治体制以及城邦运行方式上不断演进的文明。

sentences.en: and adopt, and evolve in terms of their civilization, their policy, their polities, their city-states, the way they were run.
sentences.zh: 演进的文明。

sentences.en: And of course, one can romanticize and idealize Greeks far too much.
sentences.zh: 当然，人们可能会把希腊人浪漫化和理想化得过头。

sentences.en: We know that they also had slaves, and they were brutal to their own people when they needed to be, and so on, or felt they needed to be.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们也拥有奴隶，在需要的时候对他们自己的人民也很残酷，诸如此类，或者觉得自己有必要这么做。

sentences.en: But they were unusual, and they looked at humanity, it seems, in a different way to previous civilizations.
sentences.zh: 但他们很不寻常，他们看待人类的方式，似乎与先前的文明不同。

sentences.en: Of course, we can only go from either an archaeological record and look at objects, or from a historical record when writing arrives
sentences.zh: 当然，我们只能根据考古记录来观察物品，或者根据青铜时代崩溃和腓尼基字母到来之后

sentences.en: again after the collapse of the Bronze Age and the arrival of the Phoenician alphabet.
sentences.zh: 重新出现的历史记录来了解。

sentences.en: You can start to see that the Greeks were interested in what humans were, and they wrote plays, and philosophy evolved, that examined human motive.
sentences.zh: 你可以开始看到，希腊人对人类是什么很感兴趣，他们创作戏剧，并且发展出了审视人类动机的哲学。

sentences.en: And in ways that we don't have any evidence that other people did.
sentences.zh: 其方式是我们没有任何证据表明其他人曾做过的那样。

sentences.en: And they may have done, of course, but they didn't leave it on cuneiform tablets, and they didn't
sentences.zh: 当然他们可能也做过，但他们没有把这些留在楔形文字泥板上，也没有

sentences.en: leave it in any other record for us to see clearly that they had anything like the Greeks' fascination with the ambiguity, complexity, contrariness of human motive and behavior.
sentences.zh: 在任何其他记录中留给我们清晰的证据，证明他们拥有哪怕一点类似希腊人那样对人类动机和行为的模糊性、复杂性和对立性的痴迷。

sentences.en: And that people weren't just, as I say, the early version, they weren't just four-bit blocky, non-resolved, but that people were complicated.
sentences.zh: 而且人们并不只是，正如我所说，早期版本的扁平色块、未完全成型的角色，而是人们很复杂。

sentences.en: And they had warring gods inside them.
sentences.zh: 他们内心有着交战的神明。

sentences.en: And Athens itself, and Greece, and, you know, was a confusing thing.
sentences.zh: 雅典本身、希腊，你知道的，是一个令人困惑的事物。

sentences.en: And there were different ways you could choose to live.
sentences.zh: 你可以选择不同的生活方式。

sentences.en: And you could live by your wits, or you could live by martial prowess.
sentences.zh: 你可以靠机智生活，也可以靠武力生活。

sentences.en: And the Greeks never resolved it.
sentences.zh: 而希腊人从未解决这个问题。

sentences.zh: 罗马人决定以武力为主导。

sentences.en: And they tended, they realigned Greek mythology in ways to emphasize that.
sentences.zh: 他们往往会以强调这一点的方式重新调整希腊神话。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，汤姆，你对这个的了解比我多得多。

sentences.zh: 而且你，我很乐意听你谈谈，你知道的，罗马的宗教，这比谈论希腊的宗教要容易得多。

sentences.en: Although there was a religious caste in the time of Athens, of course, they put Socrates to death.
sentences.zh: 尽管在雅典时期确实存在一个宗教阶层，当然，他们处死了苏格拉底。

sentences.en: But in, in Rome, the way they changed Ares to Mars, for example, or the way they changed Aphrodite to Venus, there were, they, the gods became symbols of a Roman attitude to,
sentences.zh: 但在罗马，他们把阿瑞斯改为玛尔斯，或者把阿佛洛狄忒改为维纳斯，神明变成了罗马人某种态度的象征，

sentences.en: didn't they more?
sentences.zh: 它们难道不是更多的吗？

sentences.en: And then you moved on to talking about Athens in, in very similar terMs. And of course, the god who joins them both is Athena, who for my money is
sentences.zh: 然后你接着用非常类似的词来谈论雅典。当然，将他们两者联系在一起的神就是雅典娜，在我看来，

sentences.en: And I think it speaks wonderfully of Odysseus, that Athena chooses him to be her favourite.

sentences.en: And I remember as a child that realising that was what was served as the gateway drug of moving from mythology to history, of thinking that the Athenians were the kind of

sentences.en: And, and Poseidon offered them spring water and, and, and all that, and, and good tides and things like that, and, and said he wouldn't send any earthquakes.
sentences.zh: 然后波塞冬向他们提供泉水、好潮汐之类的好处，并说他不会引发任何地震。

sentences.en: And Athena, apparently in this particular version, offered them the olive.
sentences.zh: 而雅典娜，在这个特定版本中，显然向他们提供了橄榄树。

sentences.en: fruit of the olive to eat.
sentences.zh: 橄榄果实可以吃。

sentences.en: And so they decided that that was a more valuable thing than anything
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为这比

sentences.en: And I soon went to the adult one, because I loved the detail of footnotes and all these extraordinary little side stories he told.
sentences.zh: 我很快就去读了成人版，因为我喜欢脚注的细节以及他讲述的那些非凡的小插曲。

sentences.en: Um, so I, I, I was sort of writing for an intelligent, young adult, early teen kind of to, uh, as much as anything.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我某种程度上是在为聪明、年轻的成年人，差不多处于青春期初期的群体写作，也是为了其他各种读者。

sentences.en: And what I had in mind, because it struck me as so important when I was first thinking about this was the, the sense of the hearth, the, the, the sitting around
sentences.zh: 我脑子里想着的是——当我最初思考这个问题时，它让我觉得如此重要——那种壁炉的感觉，那种围坐在

sentences.zh: 火堆旁的感觉，你知道的，就像许多人一样，我读过诺亚·尤瓦尔·赫拉里的书，嗯，

sentences.en: and, and had been, you know, thinking about early mankind and the development of, uh, um, early tools and then of fire and so on and of language 50,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 并且一直在思考早期人类的发展、早期工具的发展、火的出现以及5万年前语言的诞生。

sentences.en: And I was thinking, well, okay, 50,000 years ago, language and fire have allowed human beings a great deal more safety of an evening and a great deal more leisure time.
sentences.zh: 我在想，好吧，在5万年前，语言和火让人类在夜晚获得了更多安全感，也拥有了更多的闲暇时间。

sentences.en: The calories come cheaper now.
sentences.zh: 现在获取卡路里变得更便宜了。

sentences.en: And, uh, you know, animals are slowly being, uh, uh, harnessed to, to, to work in and so on.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，动物也慢慢被驯化来干活等等。

sentences.en: And so children are sitting around the fire at the end of the day and saying, as they hear the wind rustling in the trees, what is that wind?
sentences.zh: 所以孩子们在一天结束时围坐在火堆旁，当他们听到风在树林里沙沙作响时，会问：那风是什么？

sentences.en: What is that noise?
sentences.zh: 那是什么声音？

sentences.zh: 是谁在驱动它？

sentences.zh: 它从哪里来？

sentences.zh: 因为人类，每当

sentences.en: there's an agency, a force, a movement, a motive, uh, which is the same as a movement, etymologically, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 存在一个主体、一种力量、一种运动、一个动因——从词源学上讲，动因和运动是一回事，对吧？

sentences.en: Emotion.
sentences.zh: 情感（Emotion）。

sentences.en: Well, as soon as there's motion, you have to ask yourself what causes it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一旦有了运动（motion），你就得问自己是什么引起了它。

sentences.en: And that is the essence of what Newton asked, well, what causes this motion?
sentences.zh: 这正是牛顿所提问的本质：究竟是什么引起了这种运动？

sentences.en: I can't get behind it.
sentences.zh: 我无法探究其根本。

sentences.en: I can understand wind to some extent, not hugely, but there was a sense that wind had a physical explanation,
sentences.zh: 我能在一定程度上理解风，虽然不是完全理解，但有一种感觉认为风有物理上的解释，

sentences.en: wasn't a God, but everything else that moves, even what is it that pushes fruit out of the, out of twigs and, and blossom and leaves.
sentences.zh: 它不是神。但其他所有会动的东西，甚至是什么把果实从枝条、花朵和叶片中推出来。

sentences.en: And then what causes them to drop?
sentences.zh: 然后又是什么导致它们掉落？

sentences.en: And the children ask this and the adults say, Oh, well, if, if you don't know the answer, then you give, you give it an agency.
sentences.zh: 孩子们问这些问题，大人们则回答，哦，好吧，如果你不知道答案，那就赋予它一个主体。

sentences.en: And that's what we call a God.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所说的神。

sentences.en: You say, there is this force that pushes the fruit out.
sentences.zh: 你会说，正是这种力量把果实推了出来。

sentences.en: And then you, a story develops around the mother, the barley mother, Demeter, who, uh, the, the, the, the, the great goddess of fruit and food and fruit and so on, and how she
sentences.zh: 然后围绕着这位母亲，大麦之母——德墨忒尔，一个关于她的故事便诞生了。她是水果、食物以及各种收获的伟大女神，故事讲述了她是如何

sentences.en: does all this.
sentences.zh: 做到这一切的。

sentences.zh: 接着，她为什么会停下来？

sentences.zh: 为什么这一切在秋天会停止？

sentences.en: Ah, well, and then the story of, you know, so you get a, a kind of Kipling just so story, etiological stories is the technical name for them, I think.
sentences.zh: 啊，好吧，然后就有了吉卜力式的“如此这般”的故事，我想，学名应该叫病因神话（etiological stories）。

sentences.en: And, um, these are all stories that you can just, uh, tell to, to bind you as a family, a group, a clan, a tribe, a community generally abound by these stories they tell.
sentences.zh: 而且，这些都是你可以讲述的故事，用来维系家庭、群体、氏族、部落，总的来说，社区就是靠这些流传的故事凝聚在一起的。

sentences.en: And then as they trade with groups, you know, over in another valley or even across a bay, and those groups will have a slightly different story about their God.
sentences.zh: 然后，当你们与其他山谷甚至海湾对岸的群体进行贸易时，那些群体对他们的神会有略微不同的故事。

sentences.en: So you, you mix them and you get a syncretic, as they call it, sort of mixture of different religions

sentences.zh: 而且你可能记不清那个故事最初来自哪里，但所有这一切都发生在你有语言但尚未有文字的时期。

sentences.en: But then what happened is that in roughly the same time, two great Greeks, Hesiod stroke Hesiod, I never, don't ask me about vowels and Greek pronunciation.
sentences.zh: 但接下来发生的是，大约在同一时期，两位伟大的希腊人——赫西奥德，或者说赫西奥德，别问我关于元音和希腊语发音的问题。

sentences.zh: 你可以叫Hesiod，也可以叫Hesiod（译注：此处发音略有差异）。

sentences.en: Anyway, he and Homer around the same time started to give a shape that has stayed with these stories ever since.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，他和荷马在大致相同的时期，开始为这些故事赋予一种形态，这种形态自此一直伴随着这些故事。

sentences.en: And so they've become in that sense, literary.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，它们变得文学化了。

sentences.en: Um, uh, Hesiod wrote down the birth of the gods, Theogony, um, and, and gave very clear stories of who was the father and the mother and where they all came from.
sentences.zh: 嗯，赫西奥德写下了神祇的诞生《神谱》，并给出了非常清晰的故事，说明谁是父亲、谁是母亲，以及他们都来自哪里。

sentences.en: And one assumes he was working on what had been stories told orally.
sentences.zh: 人们猜测他是在口耳相传的故事基础之上进行创作的。

sentences.en: Uh, but he was self-consciously writing them down and giving them a shape.
sentences.zh: 但他是有意将其写下来并赋予其形态的。

sentences.en: And there was an authority to the way he, he, he did it, which meant subsequent generations would say, well, look up in your Hesiod.
sentences.zh: 他这种创作方式具有一种权威性，这意味着后代会说：“去查查你的赫西奥德。”

sentences.en: So, uh, by the time you get to Plato and those sort of people, they're referring to him and they're referring to
sentences.zh: 所以，到了柏拉图和那类人生活的时代，他们都在引用他的作品，并且都在引用

sentences.en: Homer, uh, um, who's given these stories and, uh, uh, an authentic shape.
sentences.zh: 荷马的作品，正是荷马赋予了这些故事真实可信的形态。

sentences.en: So they've, there's an official version.
sentences.zh: 所以它们有了一个官方版本。

sentences.en: I suppose in the same way there became an official version for the Arthur legends.
sentences.zh: 我想这就像亚瑟王传奇也有了一个官方版本一样。

sentences.en: You know, there'd been these different Chrétien de Troyes and then Mallory and others put them into, and then you
sentences.zh: 你知道的，先有克雷蒂安·德·特鲁瓦的不同版本，然后马洛里等人将它们整合，接着你就会

sentences.en: say, well, no, this is the version that the lady in the lake version with the sword coming out.

sentences.en: Um, and, or with Robin Hood, you say, this is the version here, you know, um, and they become official,
sentences.zh: 嗯，或者对于罗宾汉，你会说，这里的版本是这样的，你知道的，嗯，

sentences.en: but there's always that sense that they started with just families telling stories to keep their children amused and to tell them how the leopard got its spots as it were.

sentences.en: Yes.

sentences.en: I mean, do you have, do you have a consciousness of that?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你会有这种意识吗？

sentences.zh: 但很有趣，汤姆，这在两个方向上同时发生。

sentences.zh: 一方面，我感到完全自由，因为我认为这些是民间故事。

sentences.zh: 它们上面没有任何版权标记。

sentences.zh: 这可有点配不上你，斯蒂芬。

sentences.zh: 好吧，我是说，我能理解为什么人们会希望让这些角色显得更生动、更有活力。
